premises.text: Mobile team work needs more than email—file share, talk, and calendar—in one place because phones have become dysfunctional offices
premises.evidence_span: email doesn't really cut it for us all the time

premises.text: Zula is a structured messaging stream with in-stream file sharing, dynamic polls, and a shared-files view integrated with Dropbox and Google Drive
premises.evidence_span: we started off with a very standard messaging stream, a structured messaging stream

premises.text: Team calendar events and searchable conversation history keep work findable over long-running streams
premises.evidence_span: we can create a calendar event, calendar integration, boom. The whole team gets it

premises.text: Invites pull contacts from Zula, phone, Facebook, LinkedIn, Google+ via deep links straight into the conversation
premises.evidence_span: I can pull them in from people I met in Zula. I can pull them in from my contacts, Facebook, LinkedIn, Google+

premises.text: One-tap conference calling rings teammates with push notifications and join without phone numbers; calls can be kept/recorded
premises.evidence_span: we have one tap conference calling

domains.name: structured team messaging with files and calendar

value.text: Reduce email and get team work done through structured mobile conversation
value.evidence_span: reducing email and moving into a much more structured way of communicating as a team

causal_links.evidence_span: really helps us get things done and obviously has way reduced our email
When I invite someone to this conversation, they come straight here
I need to actually have a synchronous conversation

notes: File share, poll, and mini-Dropbox treated as facets of the structured stream (enumeration atomicity rule 1). Calendar+search kept as findability/coordination of the same stream domain. Conference calling split as separately revisable synchronous module.
